title: National Park Finder: Nearest US Parks Ranked
description: Find the nearest US National Parks to any place with the National Park Finder — 20 closest ranked by distance, map and CSV export. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a driver crossing the Midwest discovers a celebrated park sits one state away rather than 'out west somewhere' — the ranked twenty turn a someday idea into a detour decision.
quick_answer: The National Park Finder ranks the 20 nearest US National Parks to your place by straight-line distance, with a map, per-park map links and a CSV export. Search a place, click the map, or use GPS, and read the ranking — all 63 parks measured from your point, closest first.

Which parks cluster near you decides whether an annual pass pays. The CSV export feeds the family spreadsheet where these decisions live.
“Live near the parks” becomes a ranked list instead of a poster. Compare two candidate towns' twenties and the daydream gets data.
63 parks, one map: students see the system's geography — clustered in the West, scattered gems in the East — better than any list teaches it.
Distances are straight-line to the park's reference point, so a park across a mountain range ranks closer than the road will drive. The per-park map link hands you to routing for the real number.
Every congressionally designated National Park is measured — the ranking is over the complete set, so 'nearest' means nearest of all, not nearest of a sample.

faq: How is the distance measured?

Straight-line (great-circle) from your point to each park's reference location — the honest comparison metric. Road distance depends on your route; the per-park map links hand off to routing for that.
Are all 63 parks included?
Yes — the ranking measures the complete set of 63 US National Parks from your point and shows the nearest 20.
How accurate are the park coordinates?
Reference points are representative (a central or visitor location). For enormous parks the boundary can be far closer than the point — the map shows the context.
Can I export the ranking?
Yes — CSV export is built in, made for exactly the spreadsheet planning this ranking invites.
Does it use my GPS?
Only if you choose it — searching a place or clicking the map works identically, and your location is not stored.
State parks too?
This finder is the national set. State parks live in their own data elsewhere; the trails finder covers much of that ground locally.
Which entrance should I use?
The ranking does not choose entrances — park maps and the per-park links do. Big parks have several, hours apart by road.
Passes and fees?
Not covered here — the NPS site owns prices. The ranking's job is distance; the budget is a separate, worthy page.
Parks outside the US?
The set is the US system. Other countries' parks are found via the general trails and places tools.
Park anniversaries and free days?
Fee-free days are announced by the NPS yearly — the ranking does not track them; the parks' own pages do.
Territories' parks?
The 63 are the designated National Parks of the system, including American Samoa and the US Virgin Islands entries — distance-ranked from your point like all the rest.
